symbols.name: fan_out
symbols.note: Main entry point for fan-out execution; creates output directory, installs process guard, and returns run summary dict.

claims.text: DIGESTS, NOT BODIES, for the prompt: the objective carries whole file contents, and a recorder that copies them turns a 4 KB result file into a 60 KB one and duplicates the repo across runs/. The digest is what answers the questions that matter -- "did these three votes see the same prompt", "did the prompt change between runs", "is this result stale" -- and those are identity questions, which is exactly what a hash is for.
claims.why: The claim about recorder behavior and file size impact refers to code outside this chunk (a 'recorder' not shown).

claims.text: The system message IS kept whole: it is small, shared, and it was the thing nobody could see.
claims.why: No evidence in this chunk that system message is kept whole; the 'sent' dict only stores its hash and length.

claims.text: Never raises for a failing task: a fan-out of 1,200 in which one task dies must produce 1,199 answers and a named failure, not an exception. Transport failures are recorded on the result and the queue continues -- which is also why the summary reports failed separately from ok rather than folding them into a rate.
claims.why: The actual error handling and queue logic are not present in this chunk; only the docstring claim exists.

claims.text: resume skips any task whose result file already exists AND parses. A file that exists but does not parse is re-run, because a truncated result is worse than a missing one: it looks like an answer.
claims.why: The resume logic is not implemented in this chunk; no code handles file existence or parsing.

claims.text: CORROBORATION THAT CANNOT CORROBORATE IS REFUSED, not warned about. ... asking for votes you cannot get is an error at the door, where it costs nothing, rather than a dataset that has to be thrown away later.
claims.why: The code immediately following checks if any task has votes>1 and temperature<=0.0, and returns a 'refused' dict if so, refusing to run.

claims.text: At temperature 0.0 the decode is deterministic, so every vote returns the SAME answer and the agreement it produces is an artefact of counting one answer N times.
claims.why: The check if any(t.votes > 1) and temperature <= 0.0 matches this claim; the refusal message explains the same reasoning.

claims.text: A comment saying '>0 is what makes votes independent' was the only thing standing between a caller and fake agreement. This repo has a rule about that: express a restriction as a CAPABILITY, never as an instruction.
claims.why: No evidence of the previous comment or the repo rule in this chunk.

claims.text: Fail CLOSED: a fan-out whose spend cannot be capped does not run. The alternative -- proceeding unpriced and mentioning it in a summary nobody reads until the invoice arrives -- is how this went wrong once.
claims.where: comment after guard installation try block
claims.why: The code catches exceptions from install_process_guard() and returns a dict with state 'refused' and guard_error, preventing execution.

claims.text: SAME SUMMARY SHAPE as a completed run, including paid_calls and results. A refusal that returns a different dict forces every consumer to write two code paths, and the one it will forget is the
claims.why: The refusal dict shown earlier (for temperature) does not include 'paid_calls' or 'results'; the guard error return dict is not fully shown in this chunk (comment cut off).

observations.what: The 'sent' dict contains hashes and lengths of objective and system_override, but does not store the full objective or system_override.
The fan_out function signature includes many parameters with default values, including policy and system_override which are documented as 'wired through' but never called in this chunk.
The temperature check (votes>1 and temp<=0.0) returns a dict with state 'refused' and a detailed reason, but does not raise an exception.

The guard installation is wrapped in try/except and on failure returns a dict similar to the temperature refusal but with guard_error string. The comment says 'SAME SUMMARY SHAPE' but the exact keys are not fully visible (comment truncated).
The docstring claims 'Never raises for a failing task' but the actual error handling within the fan-out loop is not present in this chunk; only the guard installation and temperature check are shown.
